description:
## What

Restructure pkix-chain's top-level API around a `Verifier` struct holding prepared state (trust anchors, three-callback trust-domain seam, time). Existing free-function `verify_chain` becomes a thin wrapper preserving backwards-compat for single-call use.

Decision: PKIX-2l0v.3 = C (Mark, 2026-05-12).

## Target API shape

```rust
// New primary API
pub struct Verifier<'a> {
    anchors: &'a [TrustAnchor],
    sig_verifier: &'a dyn SignatureVerifier,
    rev_checker: &'a dyn RevocationChecker,
    aia_fetcher: &'a dyn AiaFetcher,  // when AiaFetcher lands per PKIX-fmtv.2
    now_unix: u64,
}

impl<'a> Verifier<'a> {
    pub fn new(
        anchors: &'a [TrustAnchor],
        sig_verifier: &'a dyn SignatureVerifier,
        rev_checker: &'a dyn RevocationChecker,
        aia_fetcher: &'a dyn AiaFetcher,
        now_unix: u64,
    ) -> Self { ... }

    pub fn verify_one(&self, chain: &[Certificate]) -> Result<ValidatedPath, Error> { ... }

    pub fn verify_batch(&self, chains: &[&[Certificate]]) -> Vec<Result<ValidatedPath, Error>> { ... }
}

// Preserved free function (thin wrapper)
pub fn verify_chain(
    chain: &[Certificate],
    anchors: &[TrustAnchor],
    now_unix: u64,
    sig_verifier: &dyn SignatureVerifier,
    rev_checker: &dyn RevocationChecker,
) -> Result<ValidatedPath, Error> {
    let aia = NoAiaFetcher;  // or whatever the default ends up being
    Verifier::new(anchors, sig_verifier, rev_checker, &aia, now_unix).verify_one(chain)
}
```

(Exact lifetime and trait-object vs generic-param choices are implementation-time decisions; see Open shape decisions below.)

## Why

Per AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendliness, batch, prevalidation), per the established three-callback trust-domain seam, and per prelaunch 'design for the eventual complete shape': the Verifier-as-prepared-state pattern is what the workspace ships fresh. Free-function verify_chain is the incremental-growth artifact.

This restructure brings pkix-chain in line with mozilla::pkix's TrustDomain pattern that the workspace already half-adopted (via the three callbacks). Completing the pattern is design closure, not speculation.

## Cross-cutting impact

- **PKIX-fmtv.11** (verify_tls_server design): composes Verifier internally. The eventual verify_tls_server is essentially Verifier::new().verify_one() + hostname binding via pkix-identity + DANE composition (per PKIX-j32w.3).
- **PKIX-fmtv.12** (verify_smime_signer design): same shape.
- **PKIX-fmtv.13** (verify_code_signer / verify_time_stamper / verify_ocsp_responder): same shape.
- **PKIX-fmtv.2** (AiaFetcher decision): the AiaFetcher trait shape is unchanged; it just lands on the Verifier struct as a field rather than a function argument when ready.
- **pkix-chain-simple**: separate opinionated wrapper crate; out of scope for this epic.

## Open shape decisions

(Implementation-time; not maintainer-decision-gates)

- Trait objects (`&'a dyn SignatureVerifier`) vs generic parameters (`Verifier<S: SignatureVerifier, R: RevocationChecker, A: AiaFetcher>`): trait objects ergonomic, monomorphization slightly cheaper with generics
- Lifetime parametrization: bind everything to a single `'a`, or split into multiple lifetimes? Probably one lifetime for simplicity
- Owned vs borrowed anchors: should Verifier own its anchors or borrow them? Borrow is simpler; own is friendlier for long-lived verifiers
- Default AiaFetcher placeholder: NoAiaFetcher (zero-cost no-op) is the natural default
- BuilderPattern: Verifier::builder() with chainable methods, or direct struct construction?

## Acceptance

- [ ] Verifier struct in pkix-chain with verify_one + verify_batch methods
- [ ] verify_chain free function preserved as thin wrapper
- [ ] All existing pkix-chain tests pass without modification
- [ ] Existing pkix-chain consumers (verify_chain_default, pkix-chain-simple) continue working
- [ ] PKITS regression continues passing via verify_chain (which now goes through Verifier internally)
- [ ] Documentation updated to show Verifier as primary entry point; verify_chain as convenience
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry explaining the new shape

## Out of scope

- Caching wrapper for Verifier (separate follow-on; the architecture admits it but the implementation comes later)
- Async variant (separate question)
- Migrating verify_chain callers (free wrapper preserves them)
- pkix-chain-simple restructure (separate scope)

## Cross-references

- PKIX-2l0v.3 (decision that filed this epic)
- AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache/batch/prevalidation motivation)
- AGENTS.md 'Project phase and decision framing' (prelaunch -> design for eventual shape)
- PKIX-fmtv.11/.12/.13 (verify_* wrappers that compose Verifier internally)
- PKIX-fmtv.2 (AiaFetcher; will land on Verifier struct)
title: Restructure pkix-chain: introduce Verifier struct (verify_chain becomes thin wrapper)
